root_api.initialization: Existing setup_simulation performs the same single World.reset, then initializes enabled hold helpers from actual native readback before marking the facade ready. Helpers add no physics updates or resets.
root_api.apply: robot.apply_wheel_actions(profiled_two_wheel_vector) keeps its existing signature. Disabled mode uses the original native.apply_wheel_actions wrapper unchanged. Enabled mode uses indexed native.apply_action for hold and motion.
root_api.report: robot.parking_brake_report() -> JSON-safe dict; disabled/not_initialized before helper readiness, otherwise velocity/hold/faulted with original/readback wheel gains, efforts, modes, names/indices, authored response, anchor, counters and failure.
root_api.routing: Root owns G2 selection and enables this option only for local45 PhysX. G2, canonical62 and default RTX routing were not edited here.

behavior: Verify exactly two distinct configured native wheel indices, original zero velocity Kp, finite positive wheel Kd and max effort, and force/acceleration mode readback before enabling. Reject invalid baseline or nonfinite derived gains without drive writes.
Authored response_time_s=0.2, not measured. Hold Kp=original wheel Kd/0.2; original wheel damping, effort limits and effort modes are preserved. No mode helper or effort-limit setter is used.

On the first exact two-wheel zero output, copy actual encoder angles once. Apply indexed encoder position targets AND zero velocity with positive hold gain. Repeated zero outputs reuse the same anchor without re-reading it.

On any nonzero wheel output, restore original wheel Kp/Kd before applying indexed velocity targets; clear the active anchor only after successful application. A later zero transition latches new actual encoder angles.

Public controller gain setters require full DOF arrays. Copy current full vectors and replace only the two wheel entries; validate conversion preserves other gains and original damping. Indexed action vectors preserve other joint targets. No full-DOF zero-filled wheel wrapper is used in enabled mode.

Validate input and converted target/gain arrays before writes. Read back changed gains and unchanged effort/modes before target application. Native write/readback failures propagate and fault the helper; failed transitions are not counted as successful or silently retried.

validation.scope: Nonsequential wheel indices and both force/acceleration readback; nonwheel gains/targets and physical-state preservation; one-time encoder anchor; exact nonzero release ordering/original gain restoration/re-latch; invalid baseline/target/encoder/conversion rejection; native failure accounting; default wrapper compatibility; opt-in facade routing; initialization after reset; SDK/NumPy-cold module imports.
validation.limit: Native API and arrays are substituted CPU protocols. This is not actual SDK dtype, contact, chassis-drift or brake-effect validation. No previous/full test suite repeated.

validation.action: Read the three source files, parse AST and emit SHA256. No product or SDK import.

limits: Physical effect, settling response and the force/contact cause of closed023 creep remain unverified. Root owns the bounded stationary/drive physical comparison and acceptance.
SDK API exceptions can occur after a gain write; the helper records a fault and does not claim target success or transactional rollback. Root retains runtime lifecycle ownership.
No GT input, immediate state setter, pose/encoder/odometry rewrite, kinematic lock, tolerance/TTL/clock/reservation/deadline change, or acceleration/deceleration profile change.
Only listed paths were written. No SDK/GPU/ROS/WSL/bag/Git actions, dependencies, agents, servers or persistent processes started.
